d3dev_note: d3dev is ONE Platt map per tier fitted on the StudyD3 Nexar DEV clips, which are DISJOINT from the 300 evaluation clips (overlap asserted 0), and it is used for BOTH the trigger decisions AND the scoring of the delivered stream. Because it never saw any of the 300 clips it needs no cross-fitting, and because it is ONE map per tier the per-tier monotone invariance holds exactly, so sanity check (a) passes as written. Its by_fold entries are deliberately the SAME map for all five folds, so the cross-fitted and the single-map contexts coincide.
how_to_load: by_fold[kind][fold][tier] and single_map[kind][scope][tier]. For a platt map the calibrated log-odds is a * raw_score + b and the probability is its sigmoid; for an isotonic map the probability is y[searchsorted(x, raw_score, 'left')] clipped to the end blocks. The policy library should prefer single_map['platt']['dev90'], which is fitted only on the committed D14b DEV side.
cross_fitting_note: by_fold[kind][f] is fitted on the FOUR TRAINING FOLDS of fold f and is applied to fold f's held-out clips. Five folds therefore carry five different maps, and because every metric in this row is a rank metric ACROSS clips, five different monotone maps are not one monotone map: the per-tier invariance of a single-tier arm holds for single_map and NOT for the cross-fitted application. Section 'sanity checks' of the report measures that difference rather than hiding it.
